Hi Ella — thanks for the clear ask. Drafting an acceptance checklist below that you can paste into section 4 of the MAP. Karthik and Jordan looped for numbers and ops constraints. If that works, we can add these as MAP gating items and tie them to the pilot signoff milestone.

Redwood MAP acceptance checklist (draft):
1) Baseline tokens-per-USD for pilot workload: <= $0.00035 per prompt token (measured at 8k context, running model rdx-3b-quant on Dedicated).
   - Measurement method: 30-minute steady-state run with realistic token distribution from pilot prompts; include 95th percentile latency and tokens served.
2) Latency guardrails with batching: batch sizes up to 32 allowed provided median per-request latency < 220ms and P95 < 450ms for interactive flows.
3) Prefix/KV caching enabled with dedup window of 7 days; cache-hit profiling to show >= 15% token reduction for targeted NLU paths.

Notes / assumptions: caching numbers assume warm-start (1 day of warm traffic) and that the pilot uses Redis-backed prefix cache in Dedicated. Quantization to 4-bit expected to reduce cost by ~20% vs fp16 — confirm if strict accuracy SLA is required.

Action items: Jordan to confirm batch->latency numbers for rdx-3b and provide an ops-runbook snippet; Karthik to add the exact metric names and a short script for the measurement run (we can include in the MAP appendix).

I copied procurement for visibility. If Medique wants us to tighten dollar-per-token or guarantee a specific P95, flag it and we can convert to an SLA appendix.

Thanks — I can send a clean paragraph for the MAP once Karthik confirms the numbers.

Stephanie — quick tech clarifications and proposed measurement commands. Quoting for thread:

On Sun, Mar 30, 2025 at 1:04 PM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com> wrote:
> Redwood MAP acceptance checklist (draft):
> 1) Baseline tokens-per-USD ... <= $0.00035 per prompt token ...
> 2) Latency guardrails with batching: batch sizes up to 32 allowed ...
> 3) Prefix/KV caching enabled ... >= 15% token reduction ...

My proposed refinements:
- tokens/$: We'll measure tokens consumed per 1M tokens served across the pilot traffic and divide by total billable token cost for the model variant used. For rdx-3b-quant on a T4-equivalent Dedicated slot we expect ~2.8M tokens per dollar during steady state (=> ~$0.000357 per token). Recommend we round to <= $0.00036 to give Medique a conservative band.
- batching vs latency: Default continuous-batching uses 10-20 dynamic batch size for mixed interactive traffic. If Medique has very bursty single-turn requests we should cap max batch to 16; for conversational multi-turn flows 32 is tolerable. I recommend: interactive flows -> max_batch=16; async/rerank -> max_batch=64. We can call these out per-route in the MAP.
- caching: Two levels: prefix cache (short-lived, Redis) and long-lived KV for chat contexts. For prefix cache, plan for 7d ttl and measure hit-rate via redis.metrics.cache_hits / redis.metrics.cache_lookups. Target hit-rate 12%-20% depending on prompt re-use.

Measurement commands (example):
- loadgen --profile pilot_prompts.json --duration 30m --collect_tokens --report p50,p95 --out tokens_report.csv
- python tools/compute_cost.py tokens_report.csv --model rdx-3b-quant --gpu-profile t4 -> outputs $/token estimate
